Find the $y$-intercepts of the circle $(x-3)^{2}+(y-1)^{2}=16,$ shown above.
feedback.worked_solution:
We must have $x=0$ at the $y$-intercepts. 

So, we need to substitute $x=0$ into the equation of the circle and solve for $y,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}(x-3)^{2}+(y-1)^{2} & =16 \\ (0-3)^{2}+(y-1)^{2} & =16 \\ 9+(y-1)^{2} & =16 \\ (y-1)^{2} & =7 \\ y-1 & =\pm \sqrt{7} \\ y & =1\pm \sqrt{7}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the $y$-intercepts occur at the points $(0,1-\sqrt{7})$ and $(0,1+\sqrt{7}).$
